reviews.quote: While the base MacBook Pro design is getting a bit tired, Apple's new M6 chip gives the 14-inch MacBook even more pep in its step.
exceptional battery life... lasts well over a full day (same chassis, M5 model tested)

praises: 24GB unified memory handles heavy Xcode + simulator + browser workflows without swap (r/macbook pro users)
M6 gives a solid year-over-year performance bump without changing the chassis (Tom's Hardware)
Mini-LED XDR 120Hz panel remains best-in-class for laptops (NBC)
Impeccable build quality — all-aluminum unibody (RTINGS and Tom's)
Wi-Fi 7 via Apple N1 finally standard on the Pro line (Tom's Hardware)
complaints: +$300 CAD for the 24GB tier — memory upgrades remain punishingly expensive (Tom's Hardware con)
Same 5-year-old chassis; design is starting to look stale (Tom's Hardware con)
Only 3x Thunderbolt 4 on the M6 tier; TB5 reserved for Pro/Max
RAM and SSD soldered — no upgrade path after purchase
12-core GPU still struggles with AAA games and heavy 3D renders

design_philosophy: The 14-inch MacBook Pro is Apple's pro-grade default workstation. This tier adds the RAM headroom most professional users actually need over the base config, trading a steeper upgrade price for longevity in memory-heavy dev and creative workflows.
